Independent consolidated review of the authorized generalized STR nearest, complex polygon refinement, and NativeSpatialIndex integration. - Production: packed STR build/traversal, cooperative segment BVHs, shared point/segment distance functions, NativeSpatialIndex/backend integration, public spatial-index handling, native equality, counted predicate prefixes, typed CCCL sorting/warmup, RMM allocation/stream ownership, kernel registry.
- Tests: all-family/public nearest, bounds precision, exact ties/exclusion, empty/null/logical rows, duplicate indexed views, metric edge cases, complexity padding, counted prefixes, typed-sort high bits, and allocation lifetime.

#### GPU Code Review: CLEAN

No unresolved blocking functional, precision, lifetime, or performance finding was identified. Reviewed the complete production STR/BVH kernels and launchers, their integration diff, shared metric helpers, counted-prefix changes, typed primitive dispatch, relevant native/public tests, and prior E51/E55/E61/E64/E65 correction records.

The eight-way DFS has bounded per-query scratch with feature/query admission below 2**24; segment/node admission precedes int32 extraction and four-plane offsets. Candidate generation uses outward FP32 or FP64 bounds and directed lower-bound arithmetic. Exact membership consumes the FP64 refinement context and compares terminal distances exactly, while the pruning margin only expands search. Precision-keyed kernels and both bounds variants are warmed.

The segment refiner retains component/ring containment in both directions and distributes segment traversal across a whole warp; uniform early exits preserve shuffle participation. Exact contact plus four relative endpoint projections resolves the previously incorrect near-parallel and short-segment ordering. Maximum structural complexity controls BVH admission so null/simple padding cannot conceal an outlier. Count/scan/scatter preserves all ties, int64 result offsets, stable logical IDs, deterministic lowest-ID single ties, and exclusive topological equality on device.

The reviewed root corrections remain covered: F1 metric ordering; F2 padding-dependent complexity admission; F3 logical row domain versus valid-feature size; F4 counted DE-9IM decode/transpose; F5 counted point-classifier mapping and initialized boolean tails. Cache construction and query reuse are protected by locks and readiness events. Geometry invalidation changes the native cache identity; cached owned buffers retain independent lifetimes. ## E67 pre-push review follow-up

### Verdict: FIX REQUIRED

**BLOCKING F6: nearest-only admission eagerly builds unused flat Morton state.**

The 40-byte `flat spatial index device total-bounds scalar fence` is five FP64 values: finite-row count and four global envelope extrema (`spatial/indexing.py::_device_total_bounds`). Within an actual flat Morton build this is a named, bounded planner packet. That does not justify introducing it into a different physical operation that never uses it.

`SpatialIndex._nearest_native_relation` now unconditionally acquires `_native_spatial_index_for_query`, which calls `owned_flat_sindex` and full `build_flat_spatial_index`. For already-device-resident non-grid input, that path reduces/export the five scalars, builds Morton keys and sorts an order array. Before this integration, k=1 skipped native flat acquisition; only k>1 required it. The packet in `build_right_nearest_relation` appears because the first producer has made the former query geometry device-resident before it becomes the indexed side.

`NativeSpatialIndex.nearest_relation` passes only `geometry` and `metadata.bounds` to packed STR. The STR implementation performs its own packing and consumes none of the flat index's global host bounds, Morton keys or order. Consequently the avoidable work is larger than the 40-byte transfer: nearest unnecessarily performs another layout build/sort and retains its arrays.

Independent GPU probe (1,000 point pairs, exact expected IDs and distance 0.25) compared normal full-flat acquisition with the existing device-bounds-only native carrier. Both produce identical outputs. Full flat: one five-item/40-byte packet plus the seven STR scalar fences, 54 bytes total. Bounds-only: the seven STR fences only, 14 bytes total, with no flat order or Morton-key arrays. Evidence: `e67-review-bounds-admission-probe.json`. The restored matching NVIDIA userspace library was supplied only through LD_LIBRARY_PATH; no packages, kernel, production code or hooks were changed by this probe.

### Recommended correction

Use a true lazy NativeSpatialIndex backed by owned geometry and device metadata for nearest. Reuse an existing complete flat layout when it already exists. Build/promote flat state only when a flat query or fixed-k consumer needs it. Maintain geometry/token lineage, stream readiness, locks, and packed-backend cache identity across promotion.

Do not simply store a bounds-only FlatSpatialIndex in the GeometryArray full-flat cache: general flat consumers can synthesize absent order/keys through host paths. Public orphan-array reconstruction must also avoid calling a promoting `to_flat_index()` merely to retain geometry; seed the orphan wrapper only from an already-prepared layout. Backend diagnostics must distinguish bounds-only state from actually retained Morton state.

The pipeline regression should admit only the exact existing STR scalar reasons, sizes and counts in both nearest producers, explicitly rejecting the 40-byte packet and any geometry/relation export. The fallback observability assertion should follow the actual packed-STR producer and terminal native-relation export events, retaining explicit CPU-selected behavior on CPU.

### Status

The parent accepted F6 as blocking and delegated the production correction. This follow-up supersedes the earlier LAND verdict for the newly exposed pre-push concern. A final fix review and fresh current-implementation performance/profile evidence are required; immutable CPU comparators can be reused after identity validation. No production edits, staging, commit, push or test-gate widening were performed by this reviewer.
